questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: In early Tamil texts, large landowners were called ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Vellalar
Why: Large landowners were called vellalar.
Why not the others: (B) Uzhavar were ploughmen. (C) Adimai were slaves. (D) Gahapati is a Pali term for the head of a household.
Key point: Sangam texts show sharp differences in rural society in the south.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in Ibn Battuta's life in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) He is appointed qazi of Delhi
(B) He sets out from his home in Tangier
(C) He is sent as the sultan's envoy to China
(D) He reaches Sind
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: He left Tangier in 1325 and reached Sind in 1333. Muhammad bin Tughlaq then made him qazi of Delhi, and in 1342 sent him as envoy to China.
Why not the others: (A) puts Sind before Tangier. (B) puts the post at Delhi before he reached Sind. (C) puts the mission to China before the post at Delhi.
Key point: Ibn Battuta travelled widely before reaching India.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about rebel proclamations in 1857:
(A) They appealed to all sections of the population, whatever their caste or creed.
(B) Many were issued in the name of Bahadur Shah Zafar.
(C) The Azamgarh Proclamation listed the grievances of zamindars, merchants, officials and artisans.
(D) They called for keeping British laws and courts intact.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT. The proclamations appealed to everyone, used Bahadur Shah's name and listed many grievances.
Why not the others: (D) is false. The rebels rejected British rule and its institutions. Options (B) and (D) include (D), and option (A) leaves out (B).
Key point: The proclamations looked back to the pre-British world for a vision of unity.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.sub_topic: Lords of men, horses and elephants
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Amara-nayakas
(B) Narapati
(C) Gajapati
(D) Ashvapati

List-II (Meaning)
(I) Military commanders given territories to govern
(II) "Lord of men", a popular title of the Vijayanagara rulers
(III) "Lord of horses", a title of the Deccan sultans
(IV) "Lord of elephants", the rulers of Orissa
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(I), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III)
Why: Amara-nayakas were commanders given territories (I), and narapati, "lord of men", was a title of the Vijayanagara rulers (II). The Gajapatis ruled Orissa (IV), and Ashvapati was a title of the Deccan sultans (III).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the amara-nayakas and narapati. (B) swaps narapati and Gajapati. (C) swaps Gajapati and Ashvapati.
Key point: The three titles reflect the military strengths for which each power was known.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement:
(A) The revenue demand was fixed in perpetuity.
(B) Under the "sunset law", a zamindar who failed to pay by sunset on the due date could lose his estate.
(C) The Company could revise the revenue every year.
(D) Zamindars had to pay the revenue on time even when the harvest was poor.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C) only
Why: Only (C) is false. The settlement fixed the revenue permanently, so the Company could not raise it.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correct. Options (A), (C) and (D) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: High fixed demands and strict payment rules led many zamindars to default.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: The Paharias of the Rajmahal hills practised:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Shifting cultivation
Why: The Paharias practised shifting cultivation, clearing patches of forest by burning.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not what the Paharias practised.
Key point: The Santhals, by contrast, took up settled cultivation with the plough.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: After Awadh was annexed in 1856, Nawab Wajid Ali Shah was dethroned and exiled to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Calcutta
Why: Wajid Ali Shah was exiled to Calcutta.
Why not the others: (A) Rangoon was where Bahadur Shah was later exiled. (C) and (D) were not his place of exile.
Key point: Many people in Awadh mourned the departure of their nawab.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: Small cubical blocks that the Harappans used to weigh goods were generally made of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Chert
Why: Harappan weights were usually made of a stone called chert.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were not the usual material.
Key point: The weights followed a binary system for the lower denominations.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Babur observed that in Hindustan, hamlets, villages and even towns were:
options: D) Abandoned and set up quickly
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Abandoned and set up quickly
Why: Babur wrote that villages and towns in Hindustan could be depopulated and set up again in a moment.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not what Babur observed.
Key point: Peasants moved easily when land was plentiful and conditions became hard.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.sub_topic: A land named in Mesopotamian texts
questions.question: Mesopotamian texts mention contact with a region called ____, possibly the Harappan region.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Meluhha
Why: Meluhha is probably the Harappan region. The texts mention products such as carnelian, lapis lazuli, copper and wood from it.
Why not the others: (A) Magan may have been Oman. (B) Dilmun was probably Bahrain. (C) Sumer was in Mesopotamia itself.
Key point: A Mesopotamian myth calls Meluhha a land of seafarers.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The Sufi practice of chanting a name or sacred formula in remembrance of God was called ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Zikr
Why: Zikr was the remembrance of God through the chanting of a name or formula.
Why not the others: (B) Sama was the use of music. (C) Ziyarat was a pilgrimage to a saint's tomb. (D) A khalifa was a successor.
Key point: Sufis also used music, dance and breath control.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: The Hiriya canal, one of the most striking waterworks of Vijayanagara, drew water from the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Tungabhadra
Why: The Hiriya canal drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) are other rivers of the Deccan.
Key point: The canal irrigated the valley that separated the sacred and urban cores.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: In Mahayana Buddhism, beings who were thought to have attained enlightenment but stayed to help others were called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Bodhisattas
Why: The bodhisattas stayed in the world to help others attain liberation.
Why not the others: (A) Tirthankaras are Jaina teachers. (C) Nayanars were Tamil devotees of Shiva. (D) Bhikkhunis were Buddhist nuns.
Key point: The worship of bodhisattas and images of the Buddha grew in the Mahayana tradition.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Jins-i kamil
(B) Muqaddam
(C) Patwari
(D) Kharif

List-II (Meaning)
(I) The crop season of autumn
(II) Perfect crops, such as cotton and sugarcane
(III) The village accountant
(IV) The village headman
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Jins-i kamil were the perfect crops (II), and the muqaddam was the headman (IV). The patwari kept accounts (III), and kharif was the autumn season (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps the perfect crops and the headman. (C) swaps the headman and the accountant. (D) swaps the accountant and the season.
Key point: The state encouraged perfect crops because they brought more revenue.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Al-Biruni wrote his *Kitab-ul-Hind* in:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Arabic
Why: The *Kitab-ul-Hind* was written in Arabic.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) were not its language, though al-Biruni knew several languages.
Key point: The book is divided into eighty chapters on many subjects.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the language debate in the Constituent Assembly:
(A) R.V. Dhulekar argued strongly that Hindi should be the language of the Constitution.
(B) Durgabai of Madras said that people in the south feared the propaganda for Hindi.
(C) The Language Committee proposed Hindi in Devanagari as the official language, with a gradual shift from English.
(D) The Constitution declared Hindi to be the national language.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) follow NCERT. Dhulekar argued for Hindi, Durgabai voiced the fears of the south, and the Committee proposed a compromise.
Why not the others: (D) is false. The Constitution named Hindi in Devanagari as the official language, not a national language. Options (A) and (B) include (D), and option (C) leaves out (B).
Key point: The compromise tried to balance the claims of different regions.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: The officer of the zamindar who came to the village to collect rent was the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Amla
Why: The zamindar's rent collector was the amla.
Why not the others: (A) was the village accountant in Mughal times. (C) were rich peasants. (D) were moneylenders.
Key point: Collection was difficult because ryots often could not pay.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Tobacco first reaches the Deccan
(B) Jahangir bans smoking
(C) Akbar and his nobles first come across tobacco
(D) Tobacco becomes one of the most important crops consumed in India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (C), (B), (D)
Why: Tobacco first reached the Deccan, and Akbar met it in 1604. Jahangir then banned smoking, which had no effect, and by the end of the seventeenth century tobacco was widely cultivated and consumed.
Why not the others: (B) puts Akbar before the Deccan. (C) puts Jahangir before Akbar. (D) puts the crop's spread before the ban.
Key point: New crops from the Americas reached India through trade.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Kabir:
(A) Kabir's verses are found in the *Bijak*, the *Kabir Granthavali* and the *Adi Granth*.
(B) Kabir wrote only in Sanskrit, for an audience of Brahmanas.
(C) He described the Ultimate Reality by many names, such as Allah, Khuda, Alakh and Nirakar.
(D) Some of his verses use ulatbansi, upside-down sayings.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (C) and (D) only
Why: (A), (C) and (D) follow NCERT. Kabir's verses survive in three traditions, and he used many names and upside-down sayings.
Why not the others: (B) is false. Kabir composed in a spoken language, often called sant bhasha. Options (A) and (B) include (B), and option (C) leaves out (D).
Key point: Kabir's poems are sung and remembered by people of many traditions.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Harappan diet:
(A) Fish bones have been found at Harappan sites.
(B) Animal bones show that cattle, sheep, goat, buffalo and pig were domesticated.
(C) Bones of wild species such as boar, deer and gharial have also been found.
(D) Rice was the staple grain at all Harappan sites.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (D) only
Why: Only (D) is false. Grains found include wheat, barley, lentil, chickpea and sesame. Rice is relatively rare.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correct. Options (A), (B) and (C) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: Archaeozoologists study animal bones to reconstruct diets.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: The Harappan script was probably written:
options: D) In circles round the seal
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) From right to left
Why: The script was probably written from right to left, as wider spacing on the right and cramping on the left suggest.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) do not fit the evidence of the seals.
Key point: The script remains undeciphered.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.sub_topic: The Mahayana name for older Buddhism
questions.question: Followers of Mahayana described the older Buddhist tradition as:
options: B) Bhakti, the path of devotion
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Hinayana, the "lesser vehicle"
Why: Mahayana followers called the older tradition Hinayana, the "lesser vehicle".
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were other traditions, not Buddhist labels.
Key point: Followers of the older tradition called themselves Theravadins.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: A Chinese Buddhist pilgrim of the fifth century noted that "untouchables" had to sound a clapper in the streets so that others could avoid seeing them. He was:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Fa Xian
Why: Fa Xian recorded that "untouchables" had to sound a clapper in the streets.
Why not the others: (A) Xuan Zang came in the seventh century. (B) I-Qing was another pilgrim. (D) Megasthenes was a Greek envoy.
Key point: Foreign accounts show that rules about untouchability were enforced in practice.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question: The Alvars of Tamil Nadu were devotees of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Vishnu
Why: The Alvars were devotees of Vishnu.
Why not the others: (A) The Nayanars were devotees of Shiva. (C) and (D) are not deities the Alvars worshipped.
Key point: The Alvars' compositions were compiled in the *Nalayira Divyaprabandham*.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question: Bernier described what he saw in India through a series of contrasts with:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Europe, especially France
Why: Bernier constantly compared India with Europe, especially France, usually to India's disadvantage.
Why not the others: (B), (C) and (D) were not his main point of comparison.
Key point: His account was meant to influence policy-makers in France.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: Most members of the Constituent Assembly belonged to the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Indian National Congress
Why: The Congress held the great majority of seats in the Constituent Assembly.
Why not the others: (A) The League largely stayed away. (C) and (D) had only a few members.
Key point: The Congress itself included people with a wide range of views.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question: The central story of the Mahabharata is about a war between:
options: A) Two rival kingdoms of the south
B) The Mauryas and the Kushanas
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Two groups of cousins
Why: The central story is about a war between two groups of cousins, the Kauravas and the Pandavas.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the subject of the epic.
Key point: The epic also contains many didactic sections on social norms.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology
questions.question: The Harappan civilisation is named after Harappa because it was:
options: B) The capital of a single Harappan king
C) The first site to be discovered
D) The only site with seals
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) The first site to be discovered
Why: The civilisation is named after Harappa, the first site where it was discovered.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are not the reason for the name.
Key point: Archaeologists often name a culture after the first site where it is found.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: The Mughal Empire and Agrarian Society
questions.question: Mughal emperors' hunting expeditions, which also let them hear the grievances of people in the countryside, were called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Shikar
Why: The emperor's hunt was called shikar.
Why not the others: (A) Jharokha darshan was a public appearance at a balcony. (B) Nauroz was the new year. (D) Durbar was the court.
Key point: Court painters often showed the hunt as a symbol of the ruler's care for his people.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Medieval Society through Travellers Accounts
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Visitor)
(A) Antonio Monserrate
(B) Jean-Baptiste Tavernier
(C) Manucci
(D) Abdur Razzaq

List-II (Description)
(I) A French jeweller who travelled to India at least six times
(II) A Persian envoy who visited Calicut in the 1440s
(III) An Italian who never returned to Europe and settled in India
(IV) A Jesuit priest at Akbar's court
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(IV), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(II)
Why: Monserrate was a Jesuit at Akbar's court (IV), and Tavernier a French jeweller (I). Manucci settled in India (III), and Abdur Razzaq visited Calicut (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Monserrate and Tavernier. (C) swaps Tavernier and Manucci. (D) swaps Manucci and Abdur Razzaq.
Key point: Visitors came to India as traders, priests, envoys and adventurers.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question: According to Megasthenes, the military activities of the Mauryan empire were coordinated by a committee with:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Six subcommittees
Why: Megasthenes describes a committee with six subcommittees, for the navy, transport, foot soldiers, horses, chariots and elephants.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are not the number he gives.
Key point: Accounts like his suggest a well-organised administration.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Religious History: Bhakti-Sufi Traditions
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Saint)
(A) Guru Nanak
(B) Mirabai
(C) Shaikh Ali bin Uthman Hujwiri
(D) Baba Farid

List-II (Association)
(I) His compositions were included in the *Adi Granth*
(II) Wrote the *Kashf-ul-Mahjub*
(III) A Rajput princess who accepted Raidas as her guru
(IV) Born at Talwandi, near the Ravi
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)
Why: Guru Nanak was born at Talwandi (IV), and Mirabai accepted Raidas as her guru (III). Hujwiri wrote the *Kashf-ul-Mahjub* (II), and Baba Farid's verses are in the *Adi Granth* (I).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Nanak and Mirabai. (B) swaps Nanak and Baba Farid. (D) swaps Mirabai and Hujwiri.
Key point: Hujwiri's tomb in Lahore is known as Data Darbar.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Mauryan centre)
(A) Taxila
(B) Ujjayini
(C) Tosali
(D) Suvarnagiri

List-II (Region)
(I) Orissa
(II) Karnataka
(III) The north-west
(IV) Malwa, in central India
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Taxila was in the north-west (III), and Ujjayini in Malwa (IV). Tosali was in Orissa (I), and Suvarnagiri in Karnataka (II).
Why not the others: (A) swaps Taxila and Ujjayini. (B) swaps Ujjayini and Tosali. (D) swaps Tosali and Suvarnagiri.
Key point: With the capital Pataliputra, these were the five major political centres of the empire.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Buddhist sangha:
(A) Mahapajapati Gotami was the first woman to be ordained as a bhikkhuni.
(B) Membership of the sangha was open only to Brahmanas.
(C) The *Therigatha* contains verses composed by bhikkhunis.
(D) Decisions in the sangha were reached by consensus or, failing that, by a vote.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B) only
Why: Only (B) is false. Men and women from many backgrounds, including kings, slaves and craftspeople, joined the sangha.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) are correct. Options (B), (C) and (D) all name a true statement as incorrect.
Key point: Within the sangha, all were regarded as equal once they joined.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question: The communist member who warned that the Assembly was working under the shadow of British guns was ____.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Somnath Lahiri
Why: Somnath Lahiri warned that the Assembly was British-made and working under the shadow of British guns.
Why not the others: (B) argued for stronger states. (C) spoke for tribal peoples. (D) argued for Hindi.
Key point: Lahiri urged members to free themselves from British influence.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Character)
(A) Dhritarashtra
(B) Pandu
(C) Kunti
(D) Draupadi

List-II (Relationship)
(I) Father of the Pandavas
(II) Married to all five Pandavas
(III) The blind king, father of the Kauravas
(IV) Mother of Yudhishthira, Bhima and Arjuna
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: Dhritarashtra was the blind father of the Kauravas (III), and Pandu the father of the Pandavas (I). Kunti was their mother (IV), and Draupadi was married to all five (II).
Why not the others: (B) swaps Dhritarashtra and Pandu. (C) swaps Pandu and Kunti. (D) swaps Kunti and Draupadi.
Key point: Draupadi's marriage is an example of polyandry, which was rare in Brahmanical texts.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Social Histories of Early Societies: Mahabharata
questions.sub_topic: Who could be king in the Shastras
questions.question: According to the Dharmasutras and Dharmashastras, kings were supposed to be:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Kshatriyas
Why: The Shastras said that only Kshatriyas could be kings.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) had other duties in the texts. (D) is not what the Shastras say.
Key point: In practice, rulers such as the Mauryas and Shakas came from other backgrounds.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question: The painting ____ by Joseph Noel Paton showed English women and children huddled in a circle, waiting helplessly for the end.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) In Memoriam
Why: Paton's *In Memoriam* showed English women and children waiting helplessly.
Why not the others: (A) was by Thomas Jones Barker. (B) was a cartoon from *Punch*. (C) was another *Punch* image.
Key point: British images used such scenes to stir demands for revenge.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Colin Mackenzie, who drew the first survey map of Hampi, later became the first ____ of India.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Surveyor General
Why: Mackenzie became the first Surveyor General of India.
Why not the others: (A), (C) and (D) were not his post.
Key point: His survey began the work of recovering the city's history.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part II: Vijayanagara Empire: Politics, Economy and Architecture
questions.question: Identify the incorrectly matched pair:
options: C) Saluva – founders of the empire
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Saluva – founders of the empire
Why: (C) is incorrectly matched. The empire was founded by Harihara and Bukka of the Sangama dynasty. The Saluvas came later.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (D) are correctly matched.
Key point: The Aravidu dynasty moved its capital after the battle of 1565.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: Political and Economic Systems in Early States: Inscriptional Evidences
questions.sub_topic: Order of early dynasties and events
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) Kushana rule extends over north-west India
(B) Chandragupta Maurya establishes his empire
(C) Samudragupta's prashasti is composed
(D) Ashoka fights the Kalinga war
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: Chandragupta founded his empire c. 321 BCE, and Ashoka fought at Kalinga c. 261 BCE. Kushana rule dates to the first century CE, and Samudragupta's prashasti to the fourth century CE.
Why not the others: (A) puts the Kushanas before Kalinga. (C) puts Ashoka before Chandragupta. (D) puts Samudragupta before the Kushanas.
Key point: Inscriptions and coins help fix the dates of these rulers.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Colonialism and Rural Society: Evidence from Official Reports
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of rural policies and dates or regions is incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Fifth Report – 1793
Why: (D) is incorrectly matched. The Fifth Report was submitted to the British Parliament in 1813.
Why not the others: (A), (B) and (C) are correctly matched.
Key point: The Fifth Report shaped ideas about rural Bengal for a long time.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part I: History of Buddhism and Jainism: Cultural Developments
questions.question: Makkhali Gosala, a teacher of the Buddha's time who held that everything was predetermined, belonged to the ____ tradition.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Ajivika
Why: Makkhali Gosala belonged to the Ajivika tradition, often described as fatalist.
Why not the others: (A) The Lokayatas were materialists, linked with Ajita Kesakambalin. (B) and (D) are other traditions.
Key point: The sixth century BCE saw lively debate among many teachers.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Revolt of 1857: Patterns and Representations
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.

List-I (Term)
(A) Firangi
(B) Ishtahar
(C) Danka Shah
(D) Taluqdar

List-II (Meaning)
(I) A name for Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah, "the man with the drum"
(II) A word for foreigners, used by the rebels
(III) A proclamation or notice
(IV) A landholder of Awadh
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(II), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(IV)
Why: Firangi meant foreigners (II), and an ishtahar was a proclamation (III). Danka Shah was Ahmadullah Shah's name (I), and a taluqdar was a landholder of Awadh (IV).
Why not the others: (B) swaps firangi and ishtahar. (C) swaps ishtahar and Danka Shah. (D) swaps Danka Shah and taluqdar.
Key point: The rebels' own words show how they saw British rule.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: The Making of the Constitution
questions.question:
Arrange the following in chronological order, earliest first:
(A) The Cabinet Mission proposes its plan
(B) The Government of India Act is passed
(C) B. Pocker Bahadur pleads for separate electorates in the Assembly
(D) Elections are held to the provincial legislatures
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: The Government of India Act was passed in 1935, and provincial elections were held in the winter of 1945–46. The Cabinet Mission came in 1946, and Pocker Bahadur spoke in August 1947.
Why not the others: (A) puts the elections before the 1935 Act. (B) puts the Cabinet Mission before the elections. (D) puts Pocker Bahadur's speech before the Cabinet Mission.
Key point: The provincial legislatures elected in 1946 chose the members of the Assembly.

questions.topic: Themes in Indian History Part III: Mahatma Gandhi and National Movements
questions.sub_topic: What the salt law laid down
questions.question:
Read the following source passage and answer the question that follows.

Early in 1930 Gandhi announced that he would lead a march to break the salt law. This law gave the state a monopoly over the making and selling of salt. Salt was used in every household, yet Indians could not make it even for their own use and had to buy it at a high price. By choosing salt, Gandhi turned a grievance shared by everyone into a symbol of unjust rule.

On 12 March 1930 he set out from his ashram at Sabarmati, walking towards the sea. He had told the Viceroy, Lord Irwin, of his plans in advance, but Irwin failed to grasp their importance. Large crowds gathered along the way. In village after village Gandhi urged upper-caste officials to resign their posts, and asked people to take up spinning and give up liquor.

About three weeks later he reached Dandi, on the coast, and made a fistful of salt, breaking the law. Parallel salt marches were held in other parts of the country, and thousands were arrested. The march was followed closely by newspapers in Europe and America. An American news magazine that had first mocked his thin frame soon began to describe him as a saint, and the march made Gandhi known across the world.

Question: According to the passage, the salt law:
options: A) Fixed a low price for salt in villages
B) Gave the state a monopoly over salt
C) Allowed Indians to make salt at home
D) Taxed only salt sold to Europeans
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Gave the state a monopoly over salt
Why: The passage says the law gave the state a monopoly over the making and selling of salt.
Why not the others: (A) and (C) contradict the passage. (D) is not mentioned.
Key point: Indians could not make salt even for their own use.

options: A) It was a luxury used only by the rich
B) Only peasants in Gujarat used it
C) The British did not care about the salt tax
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Every household used it
Why: Salt was used in every household, so the grievance against the law was shared by everyone.
Why not the others: (A) and (B) contradict the passage. (C) is not supported, since the state guarded its monopoly.
